authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The company completed the acquisition of a 60% equity interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center provider. This was after the fiscal year end, and Brightray's results are not in the FY2026 financial statements.
The company completed a first closing of a private placement of Purchaser Units, with gross proceeds of US$10,000,000.
A 10-for-1 forward subdivision of Class A and Class B ordinary shares was approved by the board and became effective, and the shares began trading on a split-adjusted basis.

business_model.claim: The historical operating business sells meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) services in Hong Kong. It has two service lines, event management and stage production.
quotes: Established in 2017, our operating business provides meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions, or MICE, solutions in Hong Kong.

business_model.claim: In fiscal 2026 event management brought in $5,567,719 and stage production $1,083,413 of revenue. All revenue was earned in Hong Kong from third parties.
quotes: We generated all of our revenue during the fiscal years presented in Hong Kong, from third parties, through the provision of event management and stage production services.

business_model.basis: Stated in the cited item (risk factors)
business_model.claim: The company is paid project by project, not under long-term contracts. Prices come from quotations set on a cost-plus margin basis when a project is awarded.
quotes: We offer our MICE services to clients on an individual project basis and typically do not enter into long-term contracts with them.
quotations that are formulated on a cost-plus margin basis

business_model.claim: Revenue depends heavily on one customer. The largest customer was 50.7% of fiscal 2026 revenue, against 27.9% in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Our largest customer accounted for approximately 50.7%, 27.9% and 29.1% of our revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 5.1%, from 6,328,425 to 6,651,132. Management attributes the rise mainly to event management.
quotes: The growth was mainly attributable to an increase in the number of event management projects and the larger scale of those projects.

business_model.claim: Cost of revenue has three parts: purchase costs (2,647,597), labor costs (911,134) and subcontracting costs (1,961,780) in fiscal 2026.
quotes: Purchase costs primarily consist of furniture, equipment and supplies used in the implementation of our event and exhibition projects, including costs charged by stage equipment providers and transportation costs.

business_model.claim: Gross margin fell from 31.0% to 17.0% in fiscal 2026. Purchase costs rose 62.3% while revenue rose 5.1%, and the higher costs were not fully passed on to customers.
quotes: During the year ended June 30, 2026, purchase costs increased by approximately 62.3%, while revenue increased by approximately 5.1%.

business_model.claim: Operating expenses are almost entirely general administrative expenses. They rose to $5,981,844 from $935,014, mainly because of non-cash share-based compensation of $3,979,714, and the business moved to a loss from operations.
quotes: Share-based compensation was $3,979,714 for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to nil for the year ended June 30, 2025.

business_model.claim: Demand is seasonal. It is higher around Easter, the summer holiday and Christmas, and fixed costs such as rent and staff remain in the quieter periods.
quotes: During the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, we experienced higher demands for our services during Easter, the summer holiday, and Christmas.

business_model.claim: After fiscal year-end the company acquired a 60% interest in Brightray, which provides prefabricated modular data center solutions. Brightray's results are not in the fiscal 2026 financial statements, so the historical figures describe only the MICE business.
quotes: As the Acquisition was completed after June 30, 2026, the results of Brightray are not included in our consolidated financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026 included in this annual report.

business_model.claim: Brightray's early commercial arrangements, a Macao framework agreement for about 40MW and an Indiana letter of intent for about 10MW, are non-binding. They do not create obligations to purchase or supply.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

competitive_position.claim: The historical MICE business sells on a project-by-project basis with no long-term client contracts, so clients are not obliged to rehire the company.
quotes: We offer our MICE services to clients on an individual project basis and typically do not enter into long-term contracts with them.

competitive_position.claim: Revenue is concentrated in one customer. The largest customer was 50.7% of revenue in the latest fiscal year, against 27.9% and 29.1% in the two prior years.
quotes: Our largest customer accounted for approximately 50.7%, 27.9% and 29.1% of our revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

competitive_position.claim: Revenue rose 5.1% to 6,651,132, but the gross margin fell from 31.0% to 17.0%. The filing says higher costs were not fully passed on to customers, which points to limited pricing power in the latest year.
quotes: Our gross profit margin decreased from approximately 31.0% for the year ended June 30, 2025 to approximately 17.0% for the year ended June 30, 2026.
which were not fully passed on to customers

competitive_position.claim: The company says its Hong Kong market is highly competitive with low barriers to entry, which can push prices down and cut its margin.
quotes: Relatively low barriers to entry have resulted in numerous market participants competing for similar customers and projects.
The highly competitive and fragmented market for our MICE services may continue to create adverse price pressures.

competitive_position.claim: All revenue in the years presented came from Hong Kong, so the historical business depends on local conditions.
quotes: We generated all of our revenue during the fiscal years presented in Hong Kong, from third parties, through the provision of event management and stage production services.

competitive_position.claim: Event management is the core service line, at about 83.7% of revenue in the latest fiscal year.
quotes: Our revenue derived from event management services represents approximately 83.7%, 83.4% and 80.5% of our total revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

competitive_position.claim: The company has no long-term supply contracts with its suppliers or subcontractors. It faces input-price and supplier-availability risk that it may not be able to pass on to customers.
quotes: Our Operating Subsidiaries do not enter into long-term supply contracts with its suppliers or subcontractors, so there is no assurance that they will not significantly increase the prices of their labor, materials and subcontracting charges in the future.

competitive_position.claim: After year-end the company acquired a 60% equity interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center provider. The filing says this business differs significantly from the MICE business, and its results are not in the reported financials. Any competitive position in data centers is therefore not shown by the financial statements.
quotes: As the Acquisition was completed after June 30, 2026, the results of Brightray are not included in our consolidated financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026 included in this annual report.
Brightray’s business differs significantly from our historical MICE business in Hong Kong.

competitive_position.claim: Named Brightray demand is so far non-binding. The 40MW Macao framework agreement and the 10MW Indiana letter of intent create no obligation to buy or supply.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

The principal cooperation terms of the letter of intent are non-binding and do not create any obligation to purchase, supply or pay, and the letter of intent will expire 12 months after signing unless replaced earlier by a definitive agreement.

competitive_position.claim: General administrative expenses rose to 5,981,844, and the loss from operations was 4,851,223. Share-based compensation of 3,979,714 was the first-named driver of the rise.
quotes: Share-based compensation was $3,979,714 for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to nil for the year ended June 30, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: IPO proceeds raised cash to 3,755,687 from 101,535, giving the company funds to invest. Net cash from operating activities was only 15,939.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $3,755,687 and $101,535, respectively.

financial_health.claim: Cash rose sharply over the year to $3,755,687 at June 30, 2026, from $101,535 a year earlier.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $3,755,687 and $101,535, respectively.

financial_health.claim: Short-term liquidity is positive. Current assets were $5,406,820 against current liabilities of $1,798,376, leaving working capital of $3,608,444.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, total current assets were $5,406,820 and total current liabilities were $1,798,376, resulting in working capital of $3,608,444.

financial_health.claim: Leverage is modest against equity. Total liabilities were 2,178,082 against total equity of 5,595,146. Bank borrowings were $358,021, down from $432,101. Lease liabilities are also on the balance sheet.
quotes: Outstanding bank borrowings were $358,021 and $432,101 as of June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Operating cash generation was thin. Net cash provided by operating activities was 15,939, down from 336,061 and 87,272 in the two prior years.
The fiscal 2026 loss is largely non-cash. Share-based compensation was $3,979,714 against nil in the prior year, so the cash loss is smaller than the accounting loss. Gross margin also fell sharply.
quotes: Share-based compensation was $3,979,714 for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to nil for the year ended June 30, 2025.

financial_health.claim: The cash balance came from financing, not operations. Net IPO proceeds of 5,804,648 drove net financing inflow of 5,240,035. Investing outflow of (1,612,879) was mostly deposits for investments of (1,600,000).
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, we also held $1,600,000 of refundable deposits for pending equity investments in a private company incorporated in Delaware.

financial_health.basis: stated for the classification; the coverage point is inferred from comparing balance sheet lines
financial_health.claim: All bank borrowings are classified as current because the loan agreements carry repayment-on-demand clauses. This is the debt that could fall due soonest.
quotes: The loan agreements contain repayment-on-demand clauses, and the entire outstanding balances were classified as current liabilities.

financial_health.basis: stated in the cited items; the counter is inferred from F3
financial_health.claim: Management states that cash resources, expected operating cash flows and available financing are adequate for at least twelve months, subject to uncertainties including financing access.
quotes: This assessment is subject to uncertainties, including our operating performance, customer collections, investment and acquisition requirements and access to financing.

financial_health.claim: Post year-end, the company reports a first closing of a private placement for gross proceeds of US$10,000,000. Further closings of up to 2,000,000 units were allowed by November 9, 2026.
quotes: for gross proceeds of US$10,000,000

financial_health.claim: The Brightray acquisition consideration is a non-interest-bearing P-Note settled solely in Class A Ordinary Shares. It carries no cash interest or cash principal repayment, but it is dilutive.
quotes: non-interest-bearing promissory note with an initial face amount of US$200,000,000

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (management discussion); revenue figures match F2.
growth_thesis.claim: Historical driver: the existing Hong Kong event management and stage production business grew revenue, with event management the main contributor.
quotes: The growth was mainly attributable to an increase in the number of event management projects and the larger scale of those projects.

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for the MICE business to keep growing: customers must keep commissioning projects, because the work is project-based without long-term contracts.
quotes: We offer our MICE services to clients on an individual project basis and typically do not enter into long-term contracts with them.

growth_thesis.claim: Condition: revenue depends heavily on one customer, whose share of revenue rose to 50.7% in fiscal 2026. Continued growth requires that customer to keep spending or other customers to grow.
quotes: Our largest customer accounted for approximately 50.7%, 27.9% and 29.1% of our revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

growth_thesis.claim: Prospective driver: the acquisition of a 60% equity interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center provider, extends the business beyond MICE. Its results are not in the reported fiscal-year financials.
quotes: As the Acquisition was completed after June 30, 2026, the results of Brightray are not included in our consolidated financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026 included in this annual report.

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for the Brightray driver: the company must integrate a business that differs significantly from its historical MICE business.
quotes: Brightray’s business differs significantly from our historical MICE business in Hong Kong.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1; the dilution point is from P2.
growth_thesis.claim: Condition for the Brightray driver: the seller has guaranteed minimum cumulative net profit, and any shortfall reduces the consideration. This ties the deal's economics to Brightray actually earning profit over the next three fiscal years.
quotes: DeedTech has guaranteed that such cumulative Net Profit will be not less than US$150 million, and any shortfall reduces the consideration, including, following the final determination, through the surrender of Class A Ordinary Shares previously issued in settlement of the P-Note.

growth_thesis.claim: Pipeline for Brightray: a framework agreement for a planned data center of approximately 40MW in Macao exists but creates no purchase or supply obligation.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

growth_thesis.claim: Pipeline for Brightray: a non-binding letter of intent for a planned prefabricated data center of approximately 10MW in Indiana is Brightray's first U.S. project letter of intent. Whether a purchase order followed is not shown.
quotes: The partner has indicated that it intends to issue a purchase order by November 15, 2026.

growth_thesis.claim: Funding driver: IPO proceeds lifted cash at fiscal year end, and a private placement is intended to fund Brightray's capacity expansion and working capital. Whether further placement closings happened is not shown.
quotes: We intend to use the proceeds of the Private Placement for capacity expansion and working capital requirements in connection with the expansion of the business of Brightray.
As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $3,755,687 and $101,535, respectively.

growth_thesis.claim: Possible further expansion: a non-binding memorandum of understanding to explore acquiring a holding company of film and screenplay assets is pending, and is not a commitment.
quotes: The memorandum of understanding does not constitute a definitive agreement, and the terms of any transaction, including consideration, structure and timing, remain subject to due diligence, negotiation and definitive documentation.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3; the deposit line also appears in F1.
growth_thesis.claim: Cash is also committed to refundable deposits for pending equity investments in a private company, held outside cash and working capital. Closing has been extended.
quotes: These deposits were classified as non-current assets and were not included in cash and cash equivalents or working capital.

material_events.claim: The company completed the acquisition of a 60% equity interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center provider. This was after the fiscal year end, and Brightray's results are not in the FY2026 financial statements.
quotes: The Acquisition closed on September 15, 2026, and Brightray became our consolidated subsidiary.

material_events.claim: The company completed a first closing of a private placement of Purchaser Units, with gross proceeds of US$10,000,000.
quotes: we completed a first closing of 1,000,000 Purchaser Units (10,000,000 Purchaser Units after giving effect to the Share Subdivision) for gross proceeds of US$10,000,000.

material_events.claim: A 10-for-1 forward subdivision of Class A and Class B ordinary shares was approved by the board and became effective, and the shares began trading on a split-adjusted basis.
quotes: On September 28, 2026, our board of directors approved the Share Subdivision, a 10-for-1 forward subdivision of our Class A Ordinary Shares and Class B Ordinary Shares.

material_events.claim: The company closed its Nasdaq initial public offering, with gross proceeds of approximately US$6.7 million.
quotes: The gross proceeds received from the initial public offering totaled approximately US$6.7 million.

material_events.claim: The company announced that it intends to relocate its corporate headquarters from Hong Kong to Singapore.
quotes: On September 3, 2026, we announced that we intend to relocate our corporate headquarters from Hong Kong to Singapore.

material_events.claim: The company entered a non-binding memorandum of understanding to explore acquiring PINK 308 LLC, a film and screenplay asset holding company. The acquisition remains pending.
quotes: On May 4, 2026, we entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the owners of PINK 308 LLC to explore a potential acquisition of PINK 308 LLC, a holding company being established for a portfolio of film, in-production film and screenplay assets.

material_events.claim: A Brightray subsidiary signed a non-binding framework agreement for a planned data center project in Macao.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

material_events.claim: A Brightray subsidiary signed a non-binding letter of intent for a planned prefabricated data center project in Indiana, United States.
quotes: The principal cooperation terms of the letter of intent are non-binding and do not create any obligation to purchase, supply or pay, and the letter of intent will expire 12 months after signing unless replaced earlier by a definitive agreement.

risks.basis: stated in P3 and F2 (reported figures)
risks.claim: Gross margin fell sharply in fiscal 2026 on higher purchase costs that were not fully passed on to customers, and the company posted an operating loss.
quotes: Higher purchase costs, together with increased direct labor costs, contributed to the decline in our gross profit margin from approximately 31.0% to approximately 17.0%.

risks.claim: The Brightray acquisition could dilute existing shareholders and the integration could fail. Brightray is a data center business that differs from the MICE business, and the shares issuable for the 60% interest are capped at 24,000,000 Class A shares.
quotes: Brightray’s business differs significantly from our historical MICE business in Hong Kong.

The aggregate number of Class A Ordinary Shares issuable under the Share Purchase Agreement for our 60% equity interest, inclusive of the Consideration Shares, is capped at 24,000,000 Class A Ordinary Shares (240,000,000 after giving effect to the Share Subdivision).

risks.basis: inferred from F3, F1 and P3 figures; the repayment-on-demand clause is stated in P3
risks.claim: Operating cash flow was only 15,939 in fiscal 2026, and year-end cash of 3,755,687 rested on IPO proceeds of 5,804,648 (statement tables in USD). Bank borrowings of 358,021 are repayable on demand.
quotes: The loan agreements contain repayment-on-demand clauses, and the entire outstanding balances were classified as current liabilities.

risks.claim: Revenue depends on one large customer (50.7% of revenue in fiscal 2026, against 27.9% in fiscal 2025) and on project-by-project work without long-term contracts.
quotes: Our largest customer accounted for approximately 50.7%, 27.9% and 29.1% of our revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
We offer our MICE services to clients on an individual project basis and typically do not enter into long-term contracts with them.

risks.claim: A refundable deposit of $1,600,000 for pending equity investments in a private Delaware company is outside cash and working capital. Its closing has already been pushed back to December 2026.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, we also held $1,600,000 of refundable deposits for pending equity investments in a private company incorporated in Delaware.

risks.claim: The Brightray project documents disclosed so far (Macao framework agreement, Indiana letter of intent) are non-binding and have no purchase obligations.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

risks.basis: inferred from the two figures shown in F2 and P3; the reason is not stated

quotes: Basic and diluted loss per ordinary share was $0.29 for fiscal 2026, compared with basic and diluted earnings per ordinary share of $0.05 for fiscal 2025.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the cited items; the final share count is not stated
unresolved_questions.claim: How many Class A shares will finally be issued to DeedTech for the 60% Brightray interest? The P-Note of US$200,000,000 adjusts with Brightray's Net Profit, and the share cap of 240,000,000 compares with 148,780,000 Class A shares now outstanding.
quotes: The aggregate number of Class A Ordinary Shares issuable under the Share Purchase Agreement for our 60% equity interest, inclusive of the Consideration Shares, is capped at 24,000,000 Class A Ordinary Shares (240,000,000 after giving effect to the Share Subdivision).
As of the date of this annual report, 148,780,000 Class A Ordinary Shares and 50,000,000 Class B Ordinary Shares were issued and outstanding, after giving effect to the Share Subdivision.
